contexts.text: The universe is a kind of theatre representative of the glory of the Lord...
The universe is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom; and this is a theatre representative of the Lord Himself.

Universal nature is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom in the Heavens; thence of the Lord's Kingdom on earth, or that in the Church; and thence of the Lord's Kingdom with every regenerate person. Hence it is that the universal visible world is a theatre representative of the Spiritual World.
Such theatrical scenes are then turned into direful infernal ones.
The dramatic spectacles upon the stages (in that Heaven). Explained.
Suddenly the plain on which they were standing was changed into a theatre (in which they held a discussion).
The trees on an elevated piece of ground formed as it were a theatre. Described.
The universe is like a stage, upon which are continually exhibited testimonies that there is a God, and that He is one.
Therefore the universe may be called a theatre of uses.
The Council of Nice thereby turned the Church into a theatre...
Like a player upon the stage who can personate two characters...
Like those who by theatrical things lead men away from true Divine worship; and from places of worship to playhouses.
Like players who... as soon as they have put off their theatrical garments, visit brothels.
They said, Is not the whole world like a stage on which every man acts his part?
There appeared, at Upsala, a theatre consisting of statues of a brown colour... one or two of which, like skeletons... made a beginning as if they would institute a theatrical play...

Such Spirits appear (thus)... who in externals have lived as it were in theatrical things. They supposed that those who are theatrical, and love that life, and who are like them, namely, men of external life, are such.

Those who took the way of folly, wished to enter what appeared in the shade like a palace, and behold it was a theatre of actors; and there they put on stage garments, and personated characters, and became fools.
